name: Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park
blurb: Spinifex, mulga and the desert hunters of the red centre.

tip.title: Skip the rain
tip.text: Rain and run-off feed the wildflowers, mulga and spinifex. Set Rain and rock run-off to -100% and watch the plants, then the kangaroos, rabbits and the dingoes and eagles above them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives growth for the hardy plants of the red centre, but also dries the sandplain between rains.

nodes.name: Rain and rock run-off
nodes.desc: Rainfall is low and irregular. Rain also pours off the rock domes and concentrates water and nutrients in drainage lines and at their bases.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Dry lightning and traditional Anangu burning both shape the vegetation. Some plants need fire to reproduce, while severe bushfires have burned much of the park.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals slowly in the dry soil, returning nutrients to the sandplain.

nodes.name: Spinifex
nodes.desc: Spiky hummock grasses that cover much of the red sandplain and dunes of central Australia.

nodes.name: Mulga
nodes.desc: A shrub or small tree of arid Australia that gives its name to the mulga woodlands. Listed as a dominant tree of the park.

nodes.name: Desert oak
nodes.desc: A tall, drought-tolerant tree of the sand dunes and sandplains of central Australia, frequently recorded around the park.

nodes.name: Pink mulla mulla
nodes.desc: A showy desert wildflower that blooms after rain. Galahs have been recorded eating it.

nodes.name: Harvester termites
nodes.desc: Termites eat dead plant material such as grass and wood, recycling nutrients in arid soils, and are food for ants, lizards and many others.

nodes.name: Meat ants and other ants
nodes.desc: Ants are abundant in the red centre and are the staple food of the thorny devil. Many also hunt or scavenge other insects.

nodes.name: Grasshoppers
nodes.desc: Plant-eating insects that boom after rain and feed lizards, birds and small marsupials.

nodes.name: Spinifex hopping mouse
nodes.desc: A small hopping rodent of central Australia that lives in burrows on spinifex and mulga flats. It takes plant food and is prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Galah
nodes.desc: A pink and grey cockatoo that feeds on seeds and plant material, including pink mulla mulla in GloBI records.

nodes.name: European rabbit
nodes.desc: An introduced herbivore that became a main food for dingoes and wedge-tailed eagles in central Australia, and a pressure on plants.

nodes.name: Red kangaroo
nodes.desc: The largest marsupial of the desert, grazing mostly green grasses and forbs and browsing shrubs when food is scarce. It can go long periods without drinking.

nodes.name: Thorny devil
nodes.desc: A spiny lizard that eats mostly ants and drinks by channelling dew and damp sand to its mouth. Birds and goannas prey on it.

nodes.name: Central netted dragon
nodes.desc: A common agamid lizard of the sandplain that eats insects, and is itself taken by hawks, falcons and goannas.

nodes.name: Mulgara
nodes.desc: A burrowing marsupial carnivore of spinifex deserts that eats mainly insects, as well as reptiles and small mammals. Listed as vulnerable in the park.

nodes.name: Brown falcon
nodes.desc: A widespread raptor that hunts lizards, small birds and other prey in open country; GloBI records show it taking several lizard species.

nodes.name: Dingo
nodes.desc: Central Australia's top land predator, eating kangaroos, rabbits, rodents and lizards, and carcasses in drought.

nodes.name: Perentie
nodes.desc: Australia's largest lizard, an apex predator of rocky arid country that eats reptiles, small mammals and carrion.

nodes.name: Wedge-tailed eagle
nodes.desc: A large eagle that takes rabbits, young kangaroos, lizards and birds, and feeds on carrion and roadkill.
